args.prompt_template:
We are migrating a Python script (which uses the Python `idna` package, version ~3.10) to pure JavaScript for Node.js, output in /output. Hard rules: ES Modules only (`import`/`export`, never `require`/`module.exports`); ALL files must end in `.mjs`; imports between local files must include the full `.mjs` suffix; zero external npm dependencies (only `node:` builtins allowed); STRICTLY FORBIDDEN to use or even mention Node's built-in `punycode` module or the `url`/`URL` class — everything must be reimplemented from scratch. Do not use the `python` command. You may observe reference behavior by running the precompiled executable `/workspace/dataset/test8_executable --domain X --mode encode|decode|both [--transitional V] [--strict V]` (stdout/stderr, rc).

YOUR ASSIGNED TASK (own only the files listed; other agents are concurrently writing other files with the exact interfaces given below — do not create or modify their files):

{{item}}

When done, run self-tests with `node` to verify your files (you may create scratch test files under /tmp, not /output), then report: files written, exported names, and test results.
items:
Write TWO files: /output/lib/punycode.mjs and /output/lib/idna.mjs.

== /output/lib/punycode.mjs ==
A from-scratch RFC 3492 punycode codec (bootstring params: base=36, tmin=1, tmax=26, skew=38, damp=700, initial_bias=72, initial_n=128, delimiter '-'). Exports:
- `export function punycodeEncode(input)` — takes a JS string (a single label, may contain any Unicode), returns the ASCII punycode string (NO 'xn--' prefix). Basic (ASCII) code points are copied as-is; if non-basic code points exist, append '-' + encoded tail. Must match Python's `str.encode('punycode')`.
- `export function punycodeDecode(input)` — takes the ASCII punycode string (no prefix), returns the decoded Unicode string; must match Python's bytes.decode('punycode'). In the encoded tail, uppercase A-Z count as digit values 0-25 (same as a-z). Throw an Error on malformed input (bad digit, insertion index past current length, integer overflow beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, etc.).
Test vectors (verify with node): punycodeEncode('résumé')==='rsum-bpad'; punycodeEncode('プログラム')==='qck0d2a9as'; punycodeEncode('münchen')==='mnchen-3ya'; punycodeEncode('faß')==='fa-hia'; punycodeEncode('αβγ')==='mxacd'; punycodeEncode('א')==='4db'; punycodeEncode('l·l')==='ll-0ea'; punycodeDecode('rsum-bpad')==='résumé'; punycodeDecode('4db')==='א'; round-trip random labels.

== /output/lib/idna.mjs ==
`import { punycodeEncode, punycodeDecode } from './punycode.mjs';` and reimplement the Python `idna` package's behavior (black-box reimplementation, matching these EXACT observed behaviors and error message strings; all errors are instances of the exported IDNAError):
- `export class IDNAError extends Error {}`
- `export function valid_label_length(label)` — label is a JS string; return true iff its code-point length is <= 63 (note: for a string it counts characters, not bytes).
- `export function ulabel(label)` — label may be a JS string or a Uint8Array of ASCII bytes. Behavior: (1) If it's a string, try to encode it as pure ASCII; if any char code > 127, run check_label(label) and return label unchanged. (2) Lowercase the ASCII form. (3) If it starts with 'xn--': let rest = part after the prefix; if rest is empty throw IDNAError('Malformed A-label, no Punycode eligible content found'); if rest ends with '-' throw IDNAError('A-label must not end with a hyphen'); try decoded = punycodeDecode(rest), on any throw raise IDNAError('Invalid A-label'); then check_label(decoded); return decoded. (4) Otherwise (no xn-- prefix): run check_label on the (lowercased) ASCII text and return that lowercased ASCII string. (Observed: ulabel of ASCII 'APACHE' returns 'apache'.)
- Internal `alabel(label)` (string -> Uint8Array): if label is pure ASCII: run ulabel on its bytes (this validates, e.g. hyphen rules, xn-- round-trip); if byte length > 63 throw IDNAError('Label too long'); return the ORIGINAL-case ASCII bytes (case is preserved: alabel('APACHE') -> bytes of 'APACHE'). If not pure ASCII: run check_label(label); then wire = 'xn--' + punycodeEncode(label); if its byte length > 63 throw IDNAError('Label too long'); return its ASCII bytes.
- `export function encode(domain, { strict = false, transitional = false } = {})` -> Uint8Array. transitional is IGNORED (uts46 is false in our use; accept the option and do nothing with it). If domain is empty string throw IDNAError('Empty domain'). Split domain into labels: strict ? domain.split('.') : split on the regex /[.。．｡]/u (i.e. also U+3002, U+FF0E, U+FF61). If the last label is empty, remember trailingDot=true and drop it. Map each label through alabel (errors propagate). Rejoin with '.', re-appending a trailing '.' if trailingDot. If the resulting wire byte length (excluding a trailing dot) exceeds 253 throw IDNAError('Domain too long') — this check applies ALWAYS, strict or not (verified: 253 bytes passes, 254 fails). Return ASCII bytes.
- `export function decode(domain, { strict = false } = {})` -> string. If domain is empty throw IDNAError('Empty domain'). Split labels the same way as encode (strict affects splitting the same way — verified: decode of 'a。b' gives 'a.b' normally but raises a codepoint error under strict). Handle trailing dot the same way. Map each label through ulabel, join with '.', re-append trailing '.', return the string. NO domain-length check on decode.
- Internal check_label(label) where label is a JS string; run these checks IN THIS ORDER, throwing IDNAError with these EXACT messages:
  1. empty string -> 'Empty Label'
  2. label !== label.normalize('NFC') -> 'Label must be in Normalization Form C'
  3. label[2..3] === '--' -> 'Label has disallowed hyphens in 3rd and 4th position'; else if starts or ends with '-' -> 'Label must not start or end with a hyphen'
  4. first char is a Unicode mark (category Mn/Mc/Me, i.e. matches /^\p{M}/u) -> 'Label begins with an illegal combining character'
  5. For each char (1-based position pos): if it is U+200C or U+200D (joiners) throw `Unknown codepoint adjacent to joiner U+200C at position ${pos} in ${pyrepr(label)}` (or U+200D) — implement this simplification: ALWAYS throw for joiners. Otherwise the codepoint is INVALID unless: its general category is one of Ll, Lo, Nd, Mn, Mc (test with /[\p{Ll}\p{Lo}\p{Nd}\p{Mn}\p{Mc}]/u) OR it is one of these CONTEXTO chars: U+00B7, U+0375, U+0387, U+05F3, U+05F4, U+30FB. On invalid: throw `Codepoint U+XXXX at position ${pos} of ${pyrepr(label)} not allowed` where U+XXXX is the uppercase hex codepoint padded to at least 4 digits, and pyrepr is a Python-style str repr (see below).
  6. Bidi check (RFC 5893, simplified): if no char has bidi direction R, AL or AN, pass. Direction approximation: R = Hebrew ranges (U+0590-U+05FF, U+FB1D-U+FB4F letters); AL = Arabic/Syriac/Thaana/NKo/etc ranges (U+0600-U+06FF, U+0750-U+077F, U+08A0-U+08FF, U+FB50-U+FDFF, U+FE70-U+FEFF letters/marks); AN = U+0660-U+0669 and U+06F0-U+06F9; EN = ASCII digits U+0030-U+0039; NSM = \p{M}; L = other cased/uncased letters (\p{L}); everything else = ON/ES/CS/ET. If the label contains R/AL/AN chars: first char must be R or AL, else throw `Invalid direction for codepoint at position 1 in a right-to-left label`; then every char whose direction is not in {R, AL, AN, EN, NSM, ES, CS, ET, ON, BN} (i.e. an L char among RTL) throws `Invalid direction for codepoint at position ${pos} in a right-to-left label` (verified: 'אa' fails at position 2). Also: AN and EN must not both appear; and the last char (ignoring trailing NSM) must be R, AL, EN or AN — use the same message at the offending position for these cases.
- pyrepr(str): Python repr() of a string, needed inside error messages (observed: 'RÉSUMÉ' stays literal, control chars become \x82, U+200D becomes \u200d). Implement inline in idna.mjs as a local helper (do NOT import from another lib — another agent owns /output/lib/pyfmt.mjs): quote with ' unless the string contains ' and not " (then quote with "); escape backslash, the quote char, \n -> \\n, \r -> \\r, \t -> \\t; any char whose category is in {Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, Zs} (test with /[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Co}\p{Cn}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Zs}]/u) except ASCII space is escaped: cp < 0x100 -> \xNN, < 0x10000 -> \uNNNN, else \UNNNNNNNN (lowercase hex). All other non-ASCII chars are printed literally.
- ASCII byte helpers: building Uint8Array from ASCII strings and back, implement locally.
IMPORTANT verified behaviors to honor: encode('APACHE.ORG') -> b'APACHE.ORG' (case preserved); encode('RÉSUMÉ.com') throws Codepoint U+0052 at position 1 of 'RÉSUMÉ' not allowed (uppercase non-ASCII-adjacent is invalid since only ASCII strings get lowercased via ulabel); encode('faß.de') works -> xn--fa-hia.de; 'l·l' valid; U+0640 invalid; encode('a。b') non-strict -> b'a.b'; encode('example.com.') -> b'example.com.'; encode('.') throws 'Empty Label'; decode('XN--rsum-bpad.com') -> 'résumé.com'.
Self-test your module against these cases with node, comparing to `/workspace/dataset/test8_executable --domain ... --mode both` output where useful (ignore its first two DeprecationWarning stderr lines; note its second stdout line is ulabel(encode(first_label)) which you can replicate with ulabel(encode(...))).

Rules: choose quote ' unless data contains a ' byte and no " byte (then use "); escape backslash (\\), the quote char, \t \n \r as \t \n \r; bytes 0x20-0x7E print literally; all others as \xNN (lowercase hex).

  add_argument('--domain', type=str, required=True)
  add_argument('--mode', type=str, required=True, choices=['encode','decode','both'])

- `/output/lib/pyfmt.mjs` — exports `bytesRepr(bytes)` and `strRepr(str)`

## Implementation notes

- `bytesRepr`: quote `'` unless the data has a `'` byte and no `"` byte (then `"`); escapes `\\`, the quote, `\t` `\n` `\r`; bytes 0x20–0x7E literal; everything else `\xNN` lowercase.

Covers `--name value` and `--name=value`, unambiguous prefix abbreviation (`--dom`, `--str`, `--he` all verified), generic ambiguous-option error, the "expected one argument" rule with the negative-number regex `/^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$/`, `--` separator collecting itself + rest into `unrecognized arguments` (Python 3.13 behavior, confirmed against the executable), required-before-unrecognized error precedence, invalid-choice during parse, last-occurrence-wins, and `valueString.length > 0` for `transitional`/`strict` (`--transitional False` → `true`, `--transitional ""` → `false`).
